note: CORRECTED. An earlier note here claimed a task mismatch: that MHCflurry is asked whether a peptide is presentable while our label asks whether it was observed. That was wrong. MHCflurry 2.0 trains its processing model to discriminate observed mass-spec ligands from unobserved peptides, 1:1, with 65.1% of decoys from the same protein as their hit -- substantially our task and nearly our set-C construction. These figures therefore do NOT excuse the predictor; they are the first external measurement of contamination in OUR negative class: ~1 negative in 9 looks presentable to an independently trained model, which biases every figure in this report downward.

reference.citation: O'Donnell TJ, Rubinsteyn A, Laserson U. MHCflurry 2.0. Cell Syst. 2020;11(1):42-48.e7
